source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Fusarium kernel rot (ជម្ងឺផ្សិតរលួយគ្រាប់, Fusarium Kernel Rot): this disease causes a whitish, cottony fungal growth on the surface of the ear, of a scattered/patchy pattern, and the husk often clings tightly to the ear. Diseased kernels, especially at the tip end of the ear, can show discoloration. This kernel-rot fungus can be found together with insect-damaged kernels, particularly where insect feeding has created wounds -- the fungus often develops within damaged kernels first. This condition is common when there has been heavy rain, especially where corn stands in the field have lodged (fallen over) exposing ears to weather, and the fungal spores are easily windborne to healthy ears nearby. Symptoms of true Fusarium kernel rot can sometimes closely resemble those of other kernel diseases and can be difficult to distinguish without close inspection.

Prevention and control measures:
- Use resistant/tolerant hybrid varieties.
- Choose appropriate planting dates.
- Keep the field clean of debris.
